story.head: McTavish meets his old team
paras: The Ducks (11-9-1) beat Calgary 6-1 on Sunday, while the Blues (9-9-2) lost 4-1 to Florida on Saturday. Going in, the Ducks are third in the Pacific (tied for 15th in the NHL) and the Blues seventh in the Central (tied for 20th).
The Ducks’ record (.548) is about what their chances are worth. The Blues have played better than their record (.500) says: their chances are worth about .562, and their finishing has held them back.

The Ducks are one of the league’s most physical teams (3rd) and hound the puck on the forecheck (4th). They also give up a lot of dangerous shots (31st), so the Blues could find some good looks against them. Anaheim has scored 3.76 goals a game, the fourth most in the league, and allowed 3.67, the fourth most. On the other side, the Blues ice the puck less than anyone (1st), keep things calm after the whistle (lowest) and keep dangerous shots away (2nd). Put that together and the Ducks have the edge over the Blues on physicality.

Leo Carlsson (6 G / 21 A / 27 P in 21 GP) leads the Ducks in scoring. Cutter Gauthier (18 G / 7 A / 25 P in 20 GP) has a team-high 18 goals, second in the NHL, with eight points in his last five games. Jimmy Snuggerud (10 G / 4 A / 14 P in 20 GP) is tied for the Blues’ scoring lead. Dylan Holloway (4 G / 10 A / 14 P in 20 GP) shares it.
Ville Husso (3-3-0 / .881 SV% in 5 GS) is expected to go for Anaheim. Jordan Binnington (1-3-1 / .849 SV% in 5 GS) has struggled for St. Louis so far, but is expected to start.
